conventions.convention: P and Q have finite-valued nonnegative measurable densities relative to one arbitrary measure μ; completeness and sigma-finiteness are not assumed.
Discriminators range over all measurable maps into the closed interval [0,1]. The payoff is the negative sum of two nonnegative integrals, with zero times positive infinity defined as zero.
Logarithms are natural. Set m=(p+q)/2, r=p/m and s=q/m on m>0, and r=s=0 on m=0; set φ(0)=0 and φ(t)=t ln t for t>0.
The bilinear example uses unit-step generator descent followed by discriminator ascent evaluated at the updated generator parameter, starting from a nonzero pair.

load_bearing.statement: For probability laws with finite-valued nonnegative measurable common densities, V is the negative sum of the two nonnegative logarithmic-loss integrals, and C is its supremum over all measurable D:X→[0,1], including boundary values.

For two probability measures P,Q with finite-valued nonnegative densities p,q relative to a common measure μ, the functions mφ(r) and mφ(s) are integrable, and JSμ(P,Q) is a finite nonnegative real number. It is zero if and only if P=Q, equivalently if and only if p=q μ-almost everywhere.

For probability measures with finite-valued nonnegative measurable common densities, D*=p/(p+q) on p+q>0 and D*=1/2 otherwise maximizes V over all measurable discriminators into [0,1]. C(P,Q)=−ln4+2JSμ(P,Q)≥−ln4, with equality if and only if P=Q. This asserts no convergence of finite neural alternating optimization.

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 asserts, “The functions φ,ψ are continuous on [0,2], including at 0.” The endpoint assertion requires lim(t→0+) t ln t=0, which is neither proved nor supplied by the cited facts; Step 1.1 gives only a uniform bound there. This is an elementary gap. The proof only needs Borel measurability, which also follows directly from continuity on (0,2] and the separately assigned value at zero.
